newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols pull back ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols pull back ahead of data.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options were a touch softer in late trade after edging up for a week, with activity grinding to a halt ahead of Friday's October U.S. employment report, dealers said.

"Most traders have either put on the positions they want on or gotten out of what they needed to get out of, and now it's a waiting game," said a Eurodollar trader for a brokerage firm at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME).
"After 11:30 (CST/1730 GMT) this place just died," he added. "There is no paper going through at all now."
Implied volatilities for CME January and March Eurodollar futures options were off about 0.2 point from Wednesday's closes to around 15.0 and 13.9 percent respectively.
The back end of the volatility curve was somewhat better bid as the market appeared to be pushing back its expectation on the timing of a possible Federal Reserve credit tightening.

"I think people are pretty well convinced that the Fed is going to do nothing for the rest of the year, and it's quite possible they don't do anything in the first quarter (1997)," the Eurodollar trader said.

"That's why you're seeing not only the prices of December and March (futures) trading right on LIBOR (London Interbank Offered Rate), but implied volatilities decrease there (relative to back months)," he noted.
Treasury bond option volatilities were also steady to softer as underlying bond prices drifted slightly higher.
Implied volatilities for CBOT December and March T-bond futures options stood at 11.5 and 10.2 percent respectively, marginally below Wednesday's closing levels.
"It's been a busy week, but it's starting to calm down," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Most of the large 1,000-2,000 lot deals were done early in the day, with mixed directional bias.

Among some interesting pre-payrolls strategies, an investment bank bought 2,000 legs of December 114 calls and sold 1,000 March 112 calls in a diagonal spread. Traders said it was probably aimed at achieving slightly more gamma than would result from a straight call spread, anticipating a limited rally.
Traders expected volatilities to further deflate Friday after the jobs data as most traders would likely square up their positions quickly to avoid the weekend time-decay.
Economists polled by Reuters have forecast on average an increase of 212,000 in October non-farm payrolls, against a decline of 40,000 in September.
